summary: Solifenacin succinate is a once-daily competitive M3 muscarinic antagonist for overactive bladder, reducing detrusor overactivity to relieve urge incontinence, urgency and frequency. Typical anticholinergic effects (dry mouth, constipation) occur; dose is capped at 5 mg/day in severe renal or moderate hepatic impairment and with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors.
indications: Treatment of adults with overactive bladder with symptoms of urge urinary incontinence, urgency, and urinary frequency

Do not exceed 5 mg once daily

May be taken with or without food

moa: Solifenacin is a competitive antagonist of muscarinic receptors, with relative selectivity for the M3 subtype that mediates detrusor smooth-muscle contraction. By blocking M3 receptors it reduces involuntary bladder contractions and increases bladder capacity, relieving urgency, frequency and urge incontinence in overactive bladder.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to solifenacin or formulation components (including anaphylaxis/angioedema)
relative: Decreased gastrointestinal motility (severe constipation, ulcerative colitis, myasthenia gravis)

preg: There are limited human data. Use only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: It is not known whether solifenacin is excreted in human milk; it was found in rodent milk. Avoid use during breastfeeding or weigh benefit against risk.
renal: In severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min/1.73 m2) do not exceed 5 mg once daily.
hepatic: In moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh B) do not exceed 5 mg once daily. Not recommended in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C).

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, itraconazole, ritonavir) - increase solifenacin exposure; limit dose to 5 mg/day
Drugs that prolong the QT interval - additive QT prolongation risk (avoid in high-risk patients)
moderate: Other anticholinergic agents - additive antimuscarinic effects (dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention, cognitive effects)
Drugs reducing GI motility - increased constipation/retention risk
minor: CYP3A4 inducers - may reduce solifenacin exposure (clinical significance not established)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; no clinically significant food interaction.
interactions.alcohol: Caution due to additive central nervous system depression/somnolence.

monitoring: Anticholinergic adverse effects (dry mouth, constipation, blurred vision, cognition in elderly)
Symptoms of urinary retention or worsening voiding
ECG/QT in patients with risk factors for QT prolongation
counsel: Take once daily with water, swallowed whole, with or without food
Expect dry mouth and possible constipation; increase fluids and fiber
Do not drive or operate machinery until you know how it affects you (drowsiness/blurred vision)
Avoid overheating during hot weather or exercise (reduced sweating)
Report difficulty passing urine, severe constipation, eye pain or facial/throat swelling
pk: Symptom improvement over the first weeks of therapy
Plasma peak ~3-8 hours after oral dose
Store at 20-25 C; excursions 15-30 C permitted
pearls: Cap dose at 5 mg/day with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, severe renal impairment, or moderate hepatic impairment
Avoid in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C)
Contraindicated in urinary retention, gastric retention and uncontrolled narrow-angle glaucoma
Long half-life (~50 h) allows convenient once-daily dosing but full effect/tolerability assessment takes weeks
Use caution in the elderly for anticholinergic cognitive effects and heat intolerance
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember on the same day; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip it and take the next dose at the regular time. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: Overdose can cause severe anticholinergic effects (CNS excitation, hallucinations, tachycardia, dry mouth, urinary retention). Treat with gastric lavage/activated charcoal if recent, ECG monitoring (QT), and supportive care; physostigmine may be considered for severe central anticholinergic toxicity. Manage symptomatically.
